label: def:three-calibration-discipline
title: Three-calibration discipline ($m_e$, $m_\mu/m_e$, $m_\pi$) and the calibrated substrate parameter $q_0$
html:
The QOU framework takes exactly three external calibration inputs:

Calibration Canonical observable What it fixes Numerical proxy (source)
CAL-1 m_e (leptonic mass scale) the dimensional unit (scale) m_e, CODATA (electron mass)
CAL-2 P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (neutron \beta-sector bar-skew channel) q_0 via m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}; modulus pinned most precisely by m_\mu/m_e (CODATA muon mass)
CAL-3 P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (pion-sector bar-even channel) the meson scale, independent of m_e and q_0 (meson scale independence) m_\pi, PDG (charged-pion mass)

Definition (calibrated substrate parameter). Let r = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/(m_\mu/m_e), where \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) is the hyperbolic volume of the figure-eight knot. Since 0 < r < 1, the equation

  \bigl(1 - q^{-1}\bigr)^{2} = r

has exactly one root q > 1, namely q = 1/(1 - \sqrt{r}). The calibrated substrate parameter q_0 is this root. In terms of the quantum Planck constant \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}, the defining equation reads m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_{q_0}^{2}.

This is the definition of q_0 in the ideal layer. In the Physical-Observations layer, q_0 may instead be pinned to the proton ratio m_p/m_e, which is measured more precisely. That is a substitution of the anchor, not a fourth calibration.

The definition makes no claim about how masses depend on the three inputs. The claim that every hadronic mass factors as m_e^{a}\,m_\pi^{c}\,Q_X(q_0) with Q_X \in \mathbb{Q}(q) is the conjecture Exactly three calibration inputs. The claim that the three inputs are the three real moduli of the polarised Hodge structure on H^1(\text{Bring}) = 2W is the conjecture The three calibrations are the three cohomological data of H¹(Bring).
